summary:
This law changes rules for oil and gas royalties. Royalties are payments made for taking oil or gas from land.

Sometimes oil or gas comes from an area shared by more than one lease. The government must decide how much production belongs to each lease. This law says the Secretary, the federal official in charge, must make that decision within 120 days after being asked.

While waiting for the decision, the company that holds the lease must report the oil and gas and pay royalties using the proposed sharing plan. After the Secretary gives the final decision, the company must fix its reports and payments if needed. It must do this by the end of the third month after the month it gets the decision.

The law also says the Secretary must waive interest on these royalty amounts during that time, but only if the company made full and on-time monthly royalty payments to all parties under the proposed plan.

This rule does not apply to shared oil and gas agreements that include Indian lands.
